sections.title: What this module covers
sections.body: Behavioral interview questions for Ruby developers follow the same STAR structure as any engineering role, but the best answers are anchored in Ruby and Rails specifics — the N+1 you found in production and instrumented with Bullet, the Rails 6 to 7 upgrade that broke ActionMailer previews, the Sidekiq job you wrote before you understood idempotency, the service object refactor that made the model testable. Generic answers pass the bar; Ruby-specific answers with a clear reflection beat ('looking back, I'd have added a Pact contract test before decoupling that service') stand out. This page covers the most common behavioral topics in Rails engineering interviews with STAR-structured example answers and the reflection beat that separates rehearsed from self-aware.

sections.title: Key topics and depth markers
sections.body: Topics: star-stories, failure-conflict, leadership-mentoring. Each topic has dedicated Q&A covering the concept, the comparison, the internal mechanics, and the scenario-based questions interviewers use to test production understanding.

sections.title: How interviewers probe this module
sections.body: Interviewers at Rails-focused companies probe these topics by opening with a definition question, then immediately following up with when would you use X vs Y? and what are the gotchas?. The depth marker is always the trade-off and the failure mode — not just the API surface.
